title: Release Conductor: weekly train schedule, gating heuristics, upgrade assistant and changelog composer
creator: Maya Thompson
description:
Problem: Our current weekly release process lacks a single coordinator that codifies RC tagging rules, LTS windowing, and the automated composition of release notes. Multiple teams run their own ad-hoc scripts which leads to inconsistent RC names, missed LTS pins, and manual edits across changelogs. This ticket implements a Release Conductor (scheduler + opinions) and two supporting components: an Upgrade Assistant (helper that determines upgrade-safe windows and operator notes) and a Changelog Composer (automated release-notes generator that aggregates PR labels, commit scopes, and evaluation regressions).

Goals:
- Create a canonical weekly train schedule with clear cut windows and roll-forward rules.
- Establish deterministic RC tagging semantics (semantic suffixes, backfill rules, and promotion criteria).
- Define LTS channel boundaries and automated pinning for eligible releases.
- Build a Changelog Composer that stitches PR labels, eval/regression alerts, and console metrics into a human-readable release note draft.
- Implement an Upgrade Assistant that produces pre-runbook tips (DB migration risk, client compatibility matrix) for each release.

Scope (MVP):
- Scheduler service that emits a weekly "cut window" event and produces candidate RC tag names.
- Tagging rules doc and an automated tagger GitHub Action that runs on cut events.
- Changelog Composer that consumes GitHub PRs since last tag, GroupBy labels (breaking, feature, infra, docs), and includes known regressions from automation-evals.
- Basic Upgrade Assistant that checks pinned model version compatibilities and surfaces consumer-facing upgrade notes.

Out of scope (MVP):
- Full UI in Console (follow-up).
- Multi-region rollout orchestration (follow-up).
acceptance_criteria: 1) Scheduler emits a weekly event with the next candidate RC tag in the form rc-YYYYMMDD-<minor>-<candidate> and writes to the release-conductor topic. 2) GitHub Action applies the RC tag to the release branch automatically when the tag passes gating checks. 3) Changelog Composer produces a markdown draft that groups changes by label and includes links to PRs, diffs and an evaluations appendix. 4) Upgrade Assistant produces a one-page upgrade note and a short checklist for on-call with known compatibility notes. 5) Integration tests: run end-to-end in staging and demonstrate a sample tagged RC with draft notes published to the release-notes bucket.

Write RC tagging semantics doc with examples and backfill strategy (owner: Maya)
Implement GitHub Action to tag candidate RCs and publish tag metadata (owner: EngOps)
Changelog Composer: aggregate PRs + labels, include eval regressions (owner: Release-RF)
Upgrade Assistant: compatibility checks + runbook snippet generator (owner: Platform)
Add unit and integration tests; create staging end-to-end demo (owner: QA)
comments: 2025-02-14 - Maya Thompson: Kickoff meeting notes attached. We agreed on rc tag format and weekly cut on Tuesdays 09:00 UTC. Action: Liam to prototype scheduler by 2025-02-21.

2025-02-20 - Liam Park: Prototype scheduler emits event and candidate tag names. Found edge case: if previous RC promoted on Monday, scheduler should increment candidate index rather than reuse date. Created PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/release-conductor/pull/12

2025-02-24 - EngOps (review): Suggested adding a short hash suffix for disambiguation when multiple candidate builds exist for same date. Trade-off: readability vs collision safety. Decided to include a 4-char hash as optional metadata but keep human-readable tag visible.

2025-02-28 - QA: Staging run successful; Changelog Composer included 97 PRs and an eval regression section linking to job id job-20250228-7. Need to filter infra-only bot commits. Filed follow-up ENG-50710.

2025-03-03 - Product (Aria Lopez): Requested that changelog include user-facing examples for any API changes and a short migration note if default parameters change. Added as an acceptance criteria update.
2025-03-04 - Maya Thompson: Updated description to call out Console UI as follow-up; added due date and cycle.
notes_and_decisions: Decisions: 1) RC format = rc-YYYYMMDD.<minor>.<candidate> with optional short hash stored in tag metadata; 2) LTS eligibility requires two consecutive weekly releases without regressions and explicit PM pin; 3) Changelog grouping will prioritize labels in order: breaking, feature, bug, infra, docs. Open trade-offs: whether to allow auto-promotion of RCs based on evaluation scores alone (we decided no; manual approval required for promotion).
next_steps: 1) Finish GitHub Action and run in dry-mode for two weekly cycles. 2) Add regression filter to Composer to remove infra-only commits. 3) Create a lightweight Console page colocated with Rollouts to display candidate tags and draft notes. 4) Schedule review with Security if KMS artifacts get referenced by Upgrade Assistant.
